svg.title: From Laboratory Mould to Allied Wonder Drug: The Transatlantic Penicillin Pipeline (1928–1944)
svg.desc: Historical GIS atlas map across North America, the Great Lakes, the Atlantic Ocean, Great Britain, Western Europe, and North Africa charting Alexander Fleming’s September 1928 discovery at St Mary’s Hospital, Paddington, Florey, Chain and Heatley’s 1938–41 purification and trials at the Dunn School in Oxford, the June–July 1941 wartime transatlantic mission to Peoria, Illinois (corn-steep liquor and cantaloupe Penicillium chrysogenum), $80m US government-backed deep-tank mass production by Pfizer, Merck, and Squibb in New York and New Jersey, and Allied battlefield deployment in North Africa (1943) and D-Day Normandy (June 1944, 2.3 million doses).

svg.text: EDEXCEL GCSE HISTORY • PAPER 1 (OPTION 11): MEDICINE IN BRITAIN, c.1900–PRESENT (KT4.4)
From Laboratory Mould to Allied Wonder Drug: The Transatlantic Penicillin Pipeline (1928–44)
Individual genius (Fleming 1928; Florey, Chain & Heatley 1938–41) discovered and proved penicillin, while WWII & $80m US government
funding unlocked Peoria corn-steep liquor, P. chrysogenum, and Pfizer/Merck/Squibb deep tanks—delivering 2.3 million doses for D-Day.
